correspondence.finding: The chosen eastern opening follows the mapped McClellans Creek valley westward below the Pah Rah Range, past the Quaking Aspen Road setting, to the Cottonwood Creek alluvial corridor near Sugar Loaf. The source map directly labels this tributary. The stored opening is a selected interior point and is not established as its natural source.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route turns northwest into the directly labelled Cottonwood Creek corridor and continues through the broad alluvial floor near Wilcox Ranch Road, Twin Springs Road and the Shamrock Road setting. The tributary-to-valley transition is continuous; no separate drainage divide intervenes.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The simplified selected line runs northwest across the same continuous Cottonwood Creek valley floor. The mapped intermittent thread bends farther west locally, while the selection stays on the adjoining broad low-gradient alluvial ground between valley margins. The Paiute Creek approach is lateral eastern context. This supports ordinary connected valley correspondence, not an exact match to every present channel bend or an assertion of permanent surface flow.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The corridor proceeds northwest along the labelled lower Cottonwood Creek and reaches the marsh-symbol valley floor near Grass Valley Road and Kitty Green Lane. The source map depicts the western Mullen Creek approach and the northeast-going receiving continuation within the same connected lowland. Both short selected parts lie in this common junction setting.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection turns northeast into the directly labelled Mullen Creek receiving corridor, crosses the Pyramid Highway setting, passes north of Jackass Peak and reaches the southern shore of Pyramid Lake. Part 9 contains the final landward creek passage, lake entry and initial lake-interior continuation. The creek and lake provide an ordinary connected receiving sequence across that transition.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: All remaining parts continue north and northwest wholly inside the mapped Pyramid Lake footprint and end in its interior. The lake is the terminal receiving basin, not an additional river channel. The original-source and rendered ending metadata coincide and were checked as the same lake-interior endpoint; neither the endpoint nor the generalized lake traverse is promoted to a surveyed hydrological sink or water-current path.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

findings.part_basis: Original part indices are zero-based within the sole stored fragment, and every stated span is inclusive. All 15 original parts and 89 stored positions remain in their original order. Source and rendered endpoint metadata are considered separately; no geometry repair, reversal, reconstruction or natural-headwater inference is made.

correspondence.finding: The selected opening is in a high rocky, glaciated headward trough. Its westward continuation follows the same open drainage depression into a narrow forested valley. The photographed ice, bare ground and valley sides establish the ordinary headward connection; no exact present glacier front, natural source or headstream name is assigned.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection bends northwest and then west through a continuous mountain-valley elbow. Gravelly channel reaches and the enclosing forested slopes distinguish this through-valley from adjacent hanging tributaries. The generalized line does not require a crossing into a different drainage basin.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The westward and southwestward course continues through an open, locally braided alluvial corridor beneath glaciated side valleys. Incoming tributary fans and the sinuous through-channel remain within one connected valley floor. Individual gravel bars and the modern wet thread are not treated as fixed geometry.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route follows the southwest-trending valley into a more confined forested gorge. Exposed water, alluvial patches and the incised valley floor remain connected across the narrowed reaches. Canopy and shadows limit small-channel detail without leaving a necessary valley-scale receiver unresolved.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection turns west along the receiving valley below the confined middle reach. A substantial side valley arrives from the southeast; the selected path stays on the westward continuation. The wooded valley floor and river trace support the connection across all three original parts, without assigning the tributary a name.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The westward course bends gradually northwest as the valley broadens. The connected river becomes more visibly gravelly and braided. Small offsets of the simplified line remain within the same ordinary alluvial corridor rather than implying a different branch.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The lower route follows a continuous northwest-trending braided river floor bordered by forest and steep valley sides. Multiple wet channels and bare gravel occupy one broad receiving corridor; no individual braid is equated with the complete selected part.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The river sweeps northwest and then west across an increasingly broad alluvial floor. A separate elongated dark waterbody lies north of the route, while a major valley approaches from the south near the lower junction. The selected through-corridor stays on the broad westward river and approaches the delta; the neighboring waterbody and tributaries receive no assigned names.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The last original part crosses the lower braided delta and then extends into the pale open water of the receiving lake-like basin. The separately retained source ending is on the delta/lakeshore approach; the farther-northwest rendered ending is within open water. Both definitions were independently located in the image. Their broad connection is clear without asserting a precise modern shore, current channel mouth or bank position. The retained terminal class sea is inconsistent with this photographed inland lake/delta setting and is not changed by this research.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

findings.part_basis: Original part indices are zero-based within the sole stored fragment; every span is inclusive. FID9254 parts0–27, all28parts and126positions, are retained in original order with their stage3 mainstem role. No reconstruction, repair, joining, reversal or geometry editing was performed. Source and rendered endings remain distinct.

terminal_observations.render_endpoint: Separately inspected farther northwest in open lake-like water, beyond the delta-side source ending.

terminal_observations.limit: No surveyed shoreline, exact modern mouth, lake name or data correction is claimed. The two endpoints are not collapsed.

correspondence.finding: The selected opening lies in a narrow northeast-to-southwest drainage corridor beside low rocky uplands. A darker, sinuous wash and adjoining pale alluvium continue southwest through the full first part, with small side washes joining along the way. The selected beginning is an interior point in this visible corridor, not a claimed natural headwater source. Its generalized steps stay within the same wash/valley setting.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.finding: The second part follows the southwest continuation between low ridges and alluvial slopes. Near its lower end the corridor turns west around the northern side of a larger rocky hill. The visible wash and surrounding low ground continue through the entire bend; side gullies and the nearby track do not substitute for the chosen corridor.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.finding: Parts three and four cross the west-running floor at the southern side of the central low uplands. The original clean middle image shows a continuous winding wash bordered by pale alluvium and sparse vegetation. Generalized local zigzags are sometimes offset from the darkest present trace but remain in the common low corridor, with no required crossing of a separating ridge.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.finding: The route bends northwest through a widening, pale alluvial passage. Branching washes descending from nearby uplands join this corridor, and the lower end emerges onto the broader western floor. Parts five and six and their junction are visible in the full original and middle crop. No individual side-wash hydronym or exact modern channel choice is inferred.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.component_scope: northward turn and broad lower floor
correspondence.finding: The selection turns north along the broad receiving alluvial floor and then west across its open, locally rectangular-patterned surface. The darker drainage swale, adjoining fan toes and pale plain form a continuous lowland. The selected line does not exactly follow every darker trace or field edge, but all three parts remain within this connected floor rather than crossing the surrounding rocky uplands.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.finding: Parts ten through thirteen continue west and northwest across the low, lightly mottled plain toward the eastern receiving margin of the playa. The clean western image shows the gradual transition from shallow drainage and alluvial surface into a pale, diffuse playa apron. All short stored parts and their joins were inspected; a current wet thread is not required to establish this physical continuity.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

correspondence.finding: The final three parts continue west across the broad pale playa floor, passing diffuse darker and lighter surface zones. Their complete course and separately supplied coincident source/render endpoint setting are visible. The terminal is retained near the southern interior/margin portion of the playa and is not relocated to the centre or a present water edge. The original endorheic class is consistent with the receiving-basin setting, without establishing current water balance.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: 1-based within the unchanged sole stored fragment; both span endpoints are inclusive

findings.part_basis: One-based original part numbers within the unchanged sole fragment; inclusive first/last spans.

correspondence.finding: The selected southern opening and northgoing continuation lie inside the broad mapped Deserted Glacier ice corridor. The original cartography shows a continuous glacial valley between its mountain margins through all three parts. The selection is supported as ordinary glacial-corridor correspondence; neither a surface stream on the ice nor an exact present-day glacier source or terminus is asserted.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route proceeds northeast from the mapped glacier tongue into the adjoining northward foreland drainage floor, then bends north and northwest into the broad Lowe valley. Small mapped watercourses, lowland contours and continuous valley margins support the selected transfer without an intervening divide. The source does not supply a demonstrated name for this glacial feeder, and no modern ice-front or perennial-thread requirement is imposed.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: upper lowe join and westward valley
correspondence.finding: The short northwestern join parts and long westward continuation occupy the connected upper Lowe River valley. The river is directly and repeatedly labelled on the southern side of this broad alluvial floor; northern tributaries join across it. The simplified line locally follows the northern valley margin rather than each mapped water bend, but remains in the same receiving corridor. Bench, Heiden and Wortmanns creek approaches are lateral context and are not substituted for the selected glacial feeder.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The selection continues west and southwest along the Lowe receiving valley beside the Richardson Highway, crosses the Bear Creek joining setting, and follows the narrow river/canyon passage around the mountain front into the lower western valley. Original contours and river linework show the continuous corridor through every intervening short part and the final southwest bend. Local simplified-line offsets are not treated as different river systems or exact channel positions.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route turns west into the broad lower Lowe River braidplain, passing the Browns Creek joining setting and the first selected bends among mapped braided channels and their shared alluvial floor. Every part remains within the same continuous receiving valley; a specific modern active braid or flow allocation is not inferred.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: canyon slough and lower lowe floor
correspondence.finding: These parts run west along the southern side of the common lower Lowe braidplain, including the mapped Canyon Slough corridor, then converge toward the western Lowe River tidal approach below Robe Lake. The cartography supports a continuous braided/slough/alluvial receiving floor and the named Lowe system. Canyon Slough remains a bounded component name; Robe Lake and Valdez Glacier Stream are adjoining geographic context, not upstream components substituted into the selection.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The route continues west and northwest through the lowest mapped Lowe River braidplain toward the tidal-margin opening. The original source displays connected channels, marsh ground and the adjacent broad Port Valdez waterbody. This is a continuous ordinary river-to-coast receiving setting.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.

correspondence.finding: The final part reaches the tidal mouth margin of Port Valdez. The original-source endpoint and slightly displaced rendered endpoint were examined separately on the same unmarked source crop with a private endpoint aid; both occupy the same connected tidal-mouth/receiving-water setting. Their difference does not identify a second river or require an unestablished landward transfer. Neither ending is asserted to be a surveyed present shoreline or exact active-channel mouth.
correspondence.stored_part_basis: Zero-based original part indices within this fragment.
